title: The Cosmos Fashioned as the Body, and the Body as the Field of Regeneration
arc: The teaching opens out the great correspondence between the whole cosmos and the human body, mapping the firmaments, wheels, lands and strongholds onto the parts of a cosmic-man; it then walks the five watches in which the cosmic drama played out, shows that the very same body now holds the Mind of Light and the New Man as the field of regeneration, and ends by exposing the multitude of archons embedded in that same body whose violence is felt as sickness, discharge, and death.
reading:
This chapter is a single sustained meditation on one truth: that the cosmos and the human body are built on the same plan, so that whatever is told of the heavens, the spheres, the lands, and the strongholds is at the same time being told of the man, and whatever happens in the man is happening in the cosmos. The teaching uses this correspondence first to describe how the world was made, then to describe how it is being redeemed, and finally to describe what is still being suffered in the body until the soul is released.

The opening movement reads the cosmic man from head to foot. His head corresponds to the firstfruit of the five garments — the inmost, the celestial principle from which all the lower clothings of truth descend. From neck to heart stand the ten firmaments, the fixed boundary-states between discrete degrees; the heart itself is the wheel of the sphere that sows, the will at the centre of the natural mind from which all the seeds of state are flung outward. From heart to thighs is the living air, the medium of perception that descends from the spheres to the earth; the body proper is the earth, the natural mind itself; thighs to knees are the three earths (three discrete degrees of the natural); the shins are the watch-station on which the Omophoros stands; the soles are the great earth upon which he stands, ringed by the four mountains — ordered fullness of elevated states at the ultimate plane. Within this same body the strongholds are seated: the liver is the binding-house of fire, the flesh of darkness, the sinew of water. The body is therefore a complete map of the cosmic structure in ultimates, with everything from celestial garments to bound concupiscence inscribed in it.

The teaching then moves from structure to history. It walks five watches, each ruled by a different divine governor, and at each watch a stage of the cosmic drama. In the first watch the **Pherrokatochos**, the divine Holder, exercises authority over the upper threefold heaven amid the mingling of all works; in his watch Sin tried to gush up against the icon of the Ambassador and was thrown down in shame — the restraint of evil at the highest reach. In the second watch the **King of Honor** rules over the seven lower firmaments; in his time came the earthquake of the Watchers' fall, the rational truths that descended through their own desire and were subdued by those who sent them. In the third watch **Adamas of Light** rules from the firmament downward over the sphere; in his time the abortions came down and molded the flesh — the corrupt receptivity producing the somatic form. In the fourth watch the **King of Glory** rules the three wheels; in his time motion arose in the three lands above the Omophoros, the rising-up of the three wheels of wind, water and fire — the establishment of the cyclic process of natural purification. In the fifth watch the **Omophoros** himself rules, bearing up the great land with its four extremities; in his time the lower extremities dried, the bonds were stretched, and another great earthquake came in that place — the bearing of the burden in the lowest reach. These five watches are not five chapters of past myth but five permanently active offices: restraint at the top, judicial discrimination, subduing of corrupt receptivity, cyclic turning, and patient bearing-up at the bottom.

Having shown the cosmic body in its structure and its history, the teaching makes its decisive turn. This is also the body of the **regenerate man**. In him the **Mind of Light** keeps watch over these same powers together with the **New Man**, the one who shall fill the man and bring him into the likeness of the Protomē, the face above. Each cosmic governor reappears now as an interior mystery: the Phergokatochos as the watch above the Zone, the King of Honor as the seventh heaven, Adamas of Light over against Hyle, the King of Glory turning the wheels upward toward the heaven of Life, the Omophoros (named Birah-Birē, the bond of Peace) standing in the soles in the Deep below. The teaching of Wisdom encompasses this body, looking toward the Virgin of Light, the pure receptivity who descends and shall ascend through both Zones — the upper and the lower. Love and joy, faith and truth, in which the man habitually lives, are then named as the two ships of light: the very means by which the living soul travels upward through the body, comes forth out of the Deep below, and arrives at the Height. Sun and moon, taken inwardly, are the conjugal love and faith of the regenerate, and they are how the soul gets home.

The teaching now narrows its focus from the whole cosmic-man down to "the small body," the individual man, and shows that he is structured as four cosmoses, each governed by seven archons. The first cosmos is the head with its sense-gates: two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, and the mouth. The second is from neck to chest: arms answering to the ears, breasts answering to the nostrils, the two eyes of the heart and the depth of the stomach answering to the mouth — the upper face is repeated in the chest. The third cosmos is the inner viscera, the seven inward archons of liver, bile, kidneys and the rest. The fourth is the lower body: the thighs, the loins, and the generative member from which all forms are begotten. So the four-fold cosmos is repeated four times within the man, every level a complete world with its sevenfold hierarchy of governing affections and faculties.

Onto this same fourfold body the twelve zodiac-signs are then mapped — Ram at the head, Bull at the neck and shoulders, Twins at the arms, and so down through every region to Pisces at the soles, with each sign also distributed right side and left. This is the binding wheel of natural states bound and fixed in the sphere of the stars; the demiurge of the body has multiplied and scattered them, head against foot, half against half. The point is not astrology but correspondence: every natural truth and natural affection of the man stands somewhere in this binding circuit, and the whole zodiac is the wheel of his natural states under cosmic rotation.

The teaching closes by exposing what actually inhabits this body: eight hundred and forty myriads of archons as ruling heads, organized four by four into two hundred and ten myriads of houses. These are the multitude of falsities-from-evil and corrupt affections that have made their dwellings in the natural man. While he lives they meet one another within him, rebuke and destroy one another — the inner war of the proprium against itself. When the body dies, they are released from it and are themselves struck with evil, with stripe upon blow, with burning — sicknesses inward and outward; their wounds first wrap, then pour forth a flow of saltwater and a flow of defilement (the mingled natural truth and the corruption that was bound up with it), until they are bound, drawn out through the wound, and afterwards an exchange of scraping and therapy soothes the place from which they came forth. In a single image we are shown why the body suffers: every illness, every flow, every stripe is an archon being released, judged, and either bound or healed.

Read whole, the chapter teaches that the universe is a great human form built by the Living Spirit, that the human body is that same form rewritten at the smallest scale, that the five cosmic watches are still standing as offices in every regenerate soul, that the Mind of Light and the New Man with the two ships of light (love-joy and faith-truth) carry the living soul upward through this body, and that the very flesh through which the soul ascends is also the cage of countless archons whose painful dislodging is the cost and the means of redemption. The body is therefore neither merely the cosmic icon nor merely the prison of light: it is both, and the spiritual life is precisely the working-out of that double truth.

major_images.image: Body of the cosmic man (head, neck, heart, thighs, soles)
major_images.meaning: The whole structure of love and wisdom in ultimates: the cosmos and the regenerate man share one form, so that firmaments, spheres, lands and strongholds are all parts of one Divine-Human body.

major_images.image: Five watches (Pherrokatochos, King of Honor, Adamas, King of Glory, Omophoros)
major_images.meaning: The five permanent offices of Divine governance — restraint, judicial discrimination, subduing of corrupt receptivity, cyclic turning, and patient bearing-up — through which the cosmic drama (Sin's assault, Watchers' fall, abortions' molding, motion of the three wheels, stretching of bonds) is enacted and contained.
Love-with-joy and faith-with-truth — the conjugal pair of affections (sun and moon read inwardly) by which the living soul ascends out of the Deep through the body and arrives at the Height.

major_images.image: Four cosmoses with seven archons each, and the twelve zodiac-signs distributed over the body
major_images.meaning: The complete fourfold structure of the natural-rational man, every region governed by its sevenfold order and bound by the wheel of zodiacal natural states — the field on which Mind of Light and New Man must keep watch.

major_images.image: Eight hundred and forty myriads of archons in two hundred and ten myriads of houses, releasing saltwater and defilement through wounds
major_images.meaning: The vast company of falsities-from-evil and corrupt affections embedded in the body; their inner war, their dislodging at death, and the painful purgation by which mingled natural truth and its defilement are separated and bound.
